title: Capital One Gesture Interface Patent
subtitle: A future-facing interaction concept that translated ambiguous emerging technology into a concrete, patentable product story.
summary: This sample case study shows how the new system supports hero content, structured narrative sections, a featured image viewer, and a gallery without duplicating page code.

sections.heading: Opportunity
body: The brief was not a typical feature design problem. It was an open question about how a novel gesture interface might create a differentiated banking experience without collapsing into science fiction.
For this template, the body copy is stored directly in JSON so you can revise or remove paragraphs without touching layout code.

sections.heading: Approach
body: I assembled a focused cross-functional team, mapped the interaction architecture, and turned a conceptual technology direction into a story executives and legal partners could evaluate together.

The reusable section component also supports optional bullet lists and an optional image. If a case study does not need media in a section, you can remove that object from the JSON and the layout adapts automatically.
bullets: Framed the concept around user value instead of technical novelty.
Created prototypes and storyboards to make the interaction feel concrete.
Prepared the narrative for both strategic review and legal evaluation.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: The concept helped secure internal momentum and contributed to a patent-winning direction. More importantly for the site system, this example demonstrates how the same template can hold hero media, narrative copy, metadata, feature imagery, and a flexible gallery.
Future case studies can be shorter, longer, more image-heavy, or more text-heavy by editing content files only.
